title: Login: import the browser session and X's rotating settings into one cache
description: Why: the values X rotates (web bearer, four operation ids) and the two session cookies arrive from two unrelated places, and doing that by hand is a script that rots. Scope: a 'login' verb that reads the session out of Chrome (keychain key -> PBKDF2-SHA1 -> AES-128-CBC, v10) or Firefox (one sqlite3 select), fetches X's client bundle for the bearer and the operation ids, writes one settings cache (keys are flag names, mode 0600) that every later run reads with no credential flags; --settings-path, --cookie-source, --cookie-db, --chrome-key, --web-home, --bundle-base; src/scan.bend, src/cookies.bend, src/bundle.bend; a login guide, README/CHANGELOG/ADR sections; install.sh to compile and install the CLI. Acceptance: the four login refusals fire before anything runs; a wrongly-decrypted cookie is a refusal naming --chrome-key, never a cache written with it; a run with no credentials uses the cache; login with no --settings-path works on a machine where ~/.config/bird does not exist; the e2e login case asserts what the stand-in server received, not how many requests it got.
close_reason: Login lands end to end: the browser's session, X's rotating settings, one 0600 settings cache, eleven new e2e cases and the new suites; two defects the tests could not see were found by running the installed binary by hand (the missing settings directory, and a request-count assertion standing in for a property). Landed as one commit because the login feature and its installer share one fence and the overlapping docs cannot be split without interactive staging; the installer is named in that commit. Coordination was open in the captain pane (dispatcher absent, no live fleet, zero ready beads at briefing time): no fleet tooling was live, so no reservations beyond the local toron ones and no mail were sent. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — every gate above was run, not described; fix-root-causes — the missing directory is made at the write rather than handled per caller, and the e2e assertion now checks the property instead of the tally.

title: Guard the beads ledger against row-set regressions before it is committed
description: Why: .beads/issues.jsonl is a FULL-SNAPSHOT export, so a worktree that writes it from its own older sqlite silently drops the beads another lane closed, and a closed bead then reads in_progress. This tracker has already lost gate verdicts the same way, and a lost verdict makes a close unprovable. Scope: scripts/check-beads-ledger.sh, ported from the flywheel repo's guard and adapted (bendx- id prefix, and gate rows are checked too, because that is this repo's own incident). Four passes over --base: a row that exists at base still exists; no row closed at base reads anything else; no gate-row id present at base disappears; with --history, no bead a commit subject claims to close still reads open. --ledger/--gates name the files now and are independent of where the reference is read from, so a scratch copy can be tested without silently comparing nothing. --self-test exercises the guard against its own fixtures; --force <reason> publishes a deliberate reopen loudly. Acceptance: --self-test passes every case; the real ledger at HEAD is clean; a dropped row, a reopened closed row, and a dropped gate row each exit 1 against real data; an unknown flag and a missing ledger exit 2; --base origin/main is clean.
close_reason: scripts/check-beads-ledger.sh lands: a fail-closed guard for the ledger that .beads/ is committed from, with the bendx id prefix and a gate-row pass this repo needed, because a lost verdict is what makes a close unprovable. It was watched failing on real data (a dropped row, a reopened closed row, a dropped gate verdict, and a premature close claim) as well as passing, because a gate that is only ever seen green is decoration. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — the guard's own eight cases plus four deliberate failures against the real ledger; fix-root-causes — the reference path is now separate from the file under test, which was a false OK until it was pointed at a doctored ledger.

title: X read: bookmark verb and article unfolding (chiebukuro pair)
description:
Make bird the X source for chiebukuro (sibling project). chiebukuro's chain calls twitter-cli at exactly two places:
- `twitter bookmarks -n N --yaml` (its only stream; x.rs tries twitter-cli then birdclaw then paid X API)
- `twitter tweet <id>` for a URL (reads articleTitle/articleText and quotedTweet)

bird today has no bookmarks verb, and folds an article tweet to its t.co link (live probe: `read 2030904887186514336` => text "https://t.co/cUzaPuUqJ1", lang "zxx"; the raw response carries no `article` object because bird sends empty gql features while twitter-cli sets article consumption flags).

Deliverable:
1. A `bookmarks` verb: `op_bookmarks` captured by `login` from the client bundle beside the existing four, request builder, fold into `data.tweets[]`, `--count`, help/schema, offline + e2e + live_server coverage, docs.
2. Article unfolding: article feature flags supplied through settings (`--gql-features`), and the fold reads `article.article_results.result` (title + content_state text) into the tweet body, so `read` on an article answers the article, not the link.

Acceptance criteria (checkable):
- `bird bookmarks --json` answers `data.tweets[]` and exits 0; e2e exercises the wire shape over the stand-in server; a live run against X is recorded in the close.
- `bird read <article-tweet-id> --json` answers the article title and text; a live run is recorded.
- `bend PROOF.bend`, `--check-only`, all eight offline suites, and `tests/e2e.sh` are green; guides keep `tests/e2e.sh`'s flag check green.

Out of scope: the chiebukuro-side normalizer (separate repo).
close_reason: done; commit ed01528c4562e46ef0fd23650138fa9534f47f39; verdicts unit-test-verified + live-verified (both pass rows bound to this sha); ran sh -c 'timeout 900 bend PROOF.bend && timeout 900 bash tests/e2e.sh' => ALL PROOFS CHECK, 96 cases: 96 ok, 0 failed, 0 skipped; also bend src/effects.bend --check-only and the eight offline suites (argv api http json scan bundle tweets update) => all ok; live on this sha: `read 2030904887186514336 --json` => exit 0, article_title "Claude + Obsidian: The Memory Stack That Compounds", 10440-char body (was the t.co stub); `bookmarks --count 2 --json` => exit 0, 2 tweets from data.tweets[]; deviations: op-bookmarks stays optional in `login` (the live 1.15 MB bundle carries Viewer/TweetDetail/SearchTimeline/CreateTweet but no Bookmarks record) so the recorded default is used until --op-bookmarks is set; PRINCIPLES: model-the-domain — the article body lands in the tweet's own fields (article_title + text), so a read answers one record shape instead of a second entity with its own renderer; prove-it-works — the live probe, not the design, decided the feature set: empty gql features folded an article to its link, and the flags plus fieldToggles are what X answers; boundary-discipline — the rotating flag set is a setting (`--gql-features`) with the operation ids, never compiled in, so a rotation is a config edit and the empty-{} default still reaches the operator intact.

title: Install the bird CLI on PATH as a compiled binary
description: bird currently runs only as `bend src/effects.bend -- <args>`, so every caller needs the Bend toolchain and the published release has no command of its own. Scope: compile a native binary with `bend src/effects.bend -o`, install it to ~/.local/bin/bird (already on PATH), document the install command in README and AGENTS.md, and correct the stale `sh` requirement in tests/e2e.sh. Acceptance: the installed `bird` answers `version --json` with 0.3.0 without `bend` on PATH, and the missing-attachment case still exits 2 with retryable false through the binary.
close_reason: Installed the compiled CLI: bend src/effects.bend -o bird produces a 937 KB standalone Mach-O arm64 binary in 8s, installed to ~/.local/bin/bird (already on the login PATH), with the install line documented in README and AGENTS.md. Corrected the stale POSIX-sh claim in the tests/e2e.sh header. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — the VERIFY fence runs the installed binary in a minimal environment, so the proof is the artefact the user invokes; fix-root-causes — the e2e header was corrected rather than left as a lie beside a passing suite.

principles.name: prove-it-works
principles.decision: the e2e asserts the cookie the stand-in actually received, not that the table lists a name

title: Read the X session cookies from the names the shell already exports
description: A run reads BIRD_AUTH_TOKEN and BIRD_CT0 and nothing else, so a user whose shell already exports TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN and TWITTER_CT0 (the names every guide example passes explicitly) gets no credentials at all: the tool reports auth rather than reading what is right there. Scope: add the two conventional names to the env table as fallbacks, BIRD_ still winning when both are set, log the cookie the stand-in server received so the choice is observable, and update setup.mdx, the ADR and the changelog. Acceptance: with only TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN/TWITTER_CT0 set, a mentions read against the stand-in carries that cookie, and with both spellings set the BIRD_ value is the one sent.
close_reason: TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN and TWITTER_CT0 are now read as fallbacks for --auth-token/--ct0; both spellings work, BIRD_ wins when both are set. The suite clears the credential environment first, and the stand-in logs cookie/csrf so which one won is observed rather than assumed. PRINCIPLES: prove-it-works — the wire carries the assertion, so a table entry with the wrong precedence fails the suite; never-block-on-the-human — the tool reads the environment the operator already has instead of asking them to rename variables.
